findings.claim: The text uses the phrase "interested parties" — explicitly chosen as a synonym for "stakeholders" (Ch 1.1) — and partitions them into internal (employees, owners, managers, investors, shareholders) and external (customers, creditors, suppliers, distributors, society)
findings.failure_mode: The source supports it, but the deep ref does not carry the Ch 1.1 interested-parties passage, and this distillation's stakeholder map rests on it.
findings.evidence: Source 1163-1199 (Ch 1.1, 'How Marketing Benefits the Organization, Its Interested Parties, and Society'): interested parties 'can be categorized into two types: internal and external ... You may see these people and groups referred to as "stakeholders"'; internal = 'employees, owners, managers, and investors (shareholders)'; external = 'customers, creditors, suppliers, distributors, and even society at large'. No 'interested parties' anywhere in the deep ref.
findings.fix: cycle-to-deep: add to deep Part I a Ch 1.1 paragraph: 'Interested parties are those persons or entities that have an interest in the success or failure of a company' [V], split into internal (employees, owners, managers, investors/shareholders) and external (customers, creditors, suppliers, distributors, society), 'referred to as "stakeholders" in business writing' [V]. correct (line 8): 'explicitly chosen as a synonym' -> 'which the text notes are called "stakeholders" in business writing'.

findings.claim: Internal marketing. Promoting the objectives, products, and services of a company to its own employees — recognising employees as the first stakeholder group. (Source: Ch 1.1; Ch 13.5) / employees as internal customers (... Ch 13.5 internal marketing)
findings.failure_mode: Mis-cited: Ch 13.5 (ethics in marketing communication) has no internal-marketing content. 'The first stakeholder group' is the distillation's flourish. The Ch 1.1 definition is source-supported, but the deep ref carries internal marketing only as a leg of the Service Marketing Triangle (Ch 11.2).
findings.evidence: Source 1185-1187 (Ch 1.1): 'Internal marketing involves promoting the objectives, products, and services of a company to its internal constituents—particularly employees.' grep 'internal marketing' in the source: 1185, 1193 (Ch 1.1), 22618 (Ch 11.2), none in Ch 13.5 (26861-27413). Deep 293: internal marketing as a Triangle leg.
findings.fix: correct: Internal marketing. Promoting the objectives, products, and services of a company to its internal constituents, particularly employees. (Source: Ch 1.1; Ch 11.2). In line 8, replace 'Ch 13.5 internal marketing' with 'Ch 1.1 internal marketing'. cycle-to-deep: add the Ch 1.1 definition to the deep ref.

findings.claim: the planet itself, treated as a stakeholder via the ESG framework (Ch 19) / Three pillars / ESG ... — the three groups of stakeholders sustainability serves
findings.failure_mode: The source's three pillars are dimensions of sustainability, not stakeholder groups, and the planet is not in its stakeholder list.
findings.evidence: Deep 487: three pillars / 'planet, people, profits' = environmental, social, economic/governance. Deep 493, source 37793-37795: stakeholders = 'customers, shareholders, employees, vendors, interest groups, media, and the general public'.
findings.fix: correct (8): ... and, in the closing chapter, the environment as one of three sustainability pillars alongside social and economic/governance (Ch 19). correct (42): Environmental, social, economic/governance — the three dimensions sustainable marketing is measured against (Ch 19.1).

findings.claim: Are we responsive within the 30–60-minute window consumers expect?
findings.failure_mode: Overstates a survey result as a universal expectation, and the deep ref doesn't carry it. The source reports that 42 per cent expect a reply within 60 minutes and 32 per cent within 30.

findings.fix: correct: Are we answering fast enough? (The source cites research that 42 per cent of consumers expect an email reply within 60 minutes and 32 per cent within 30, Ch 1.7.) cycle-to-deep: add the statistic to deep Ch 1.7.

findings.section: Questions, Phase 6 (Channel-member relationships; also line 109, Channel partner motivation)
findings.claim: collaborative, transparent, cohesive relationships with intermediaries / bonuses, incentives, sales materials, samples, training, dealer conferences
findings.failure_mode: The source supports both (Ch 17.4 'Managing and Motivating Channel Members'), but the deep ref carries no Ch 17.4 management/motivation content.

The deep ref carries neither statement.

findings.claim: PR-crisis denial — defending the indefensible (Toyota acceleration; Pepsi Kendall Jenner; Nivea "White Is Purity").
findings.failure_mode: Nivea did not defend its campaign: the source says it apologized and removed it. The source presents Pepsi as a diversity-marketing misstep that drew backlash, not a denial (the Pepsi case is not in the deep ref). Only Toyota fits.
findings.evidence: Source 13720-13726 (Ch 7.1): Nivea 'apologized and removed the campaign'. Source 15870-15875 (Ch 8.2): Pepsi's campaign 'received heavy backlash ... described as insensitive and offensive'; note 12 is headlined 'Pepsi Pulls Controversial Kendall Jenner Ad'. Deep 86: Toyota as the cost of cover-up (Ch 2.5).
findings.fix: correct: *PR-crisis denial* — defending the indefensible (Toyota's unintended-acceleration cover-up and $1.2 billion fine, Ch 2.5). Move Pepsi and Nivea to a separate anti-pattern: *Culturally insensitive campaigns that reach the public* (Nivea 'White Is Purity', Ch 7.1; Pepsi's Kendall Jenner ad, Ch 8.2).

findings.claim: The service-profit chain is parallel to the OB literature on engagement, with Argyris's basic-incongruity thesis lurking beneath the internal service quality link.

notes: derived-from-deep sha256 matches the current deep ref. All [V] quotations match the converted source word for word after normalisation (2215, 2311, 37656, 37800, 33356, 2411). The distillation leans on source passages the deep ref never carried: Ch 1.1 interested parties and internal marketing, the Ch 1.6 CRM 'two-way street', the Ch 15.3 'real work begins', the Ch 17.4 channel-management qualities, the Ch 1.7 response-time statistic, the Ch 8.3 Texican Whopper, and the Ch 8.4 acculturation-by-birthplace sentence. That means the projection re-read the source (a protocol breach), and the deep ref's coverage of Ch 1.1 and Ch 17.4 is thin; T001-T014 and T023 carry cycle-to-deep fixes. Multi-claim findings: T001, T002, T003, T004, T006, T009, T011, T015 and T020 count two claims each. Checked and faithful: exchange-process components (buyer, desired object, seller: source 2219-2238); Gap 4 = communication gap (source 22729); crisis communication in Ch 14.4 (source 28178); the Bombas give-with-purchase framing (source 38146-38149); the HUD-Facebook, Toyota, Tylenol, Walmart and Patagonia examples; the Hofstede count note (deep 574); and every borrowed-through entry except Ries & Trout (Kotler, AMA, Hofstede, PZB, Hall, Hsieh, Transparency International, Chouinard).
